transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-30 14:00 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Evan (Redwood AE), Samira (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood CSM), Dr. Aaron Patel, Maya Chen, Luke Howard, Sofia Ramos (Novamed)

Summary (auto-generated, may be imperfect):
Redwood and Novamed reviewed POC success criteria and scoped a quality evaluation plan focused on hallucination rate, format adherence, and regression tests. Agreement to exchange golden prompts and sample dataset; Redwood to run benchmarks across hosted and dedicated options and propose scoring weights. Security and timeline questions noted.

Topics:
- Success criteria (accuracy, hallucination, latency, cost)
- Workload sizing and benchmark scale
- Golden prompts and regression test design
- Hallucination and format checks
- Scoring approach and pass/fail thresholds
- Timeline and next steps

Transcript:
[00:00] Evan Martinez: hey everyone thanks for joining on time, i know we have an hour. quick intro i m evan with Redwood inference, im the ae on this account, and with me is samira our solutions engineer.
[00:12] Dr. Aaron Patel: thanks, Aaron here, chief data officer at Novamed. we are evaluating LLM assist for clinical chart summarization and patient Q&A. main concerns are hallucinations and PHI handling.
[00:22] Maya Chen: hi i m maya product, timeline is Q3 pilot, want to validate quality before we commit compute budget.
[00:28] Samira Lopez: great, on our side we want to make sure the POC has clear eval metrics — golden prompts, regression tests, and hallucination/format checks, which is what we are here to scope.
[00:36] Luke Howard: Luke, eng on the integration side; we ll own dataset extraction and infra for the pilot.
[00:41] Sofia Ramos: Sofia from compliance, will want to see audit logs, KMS usage, and retention policies before any dedicated deployment.
[00:48] Evan Martinez: perfect. quick agenda: align on success criteria, agree dataset and workload size, define golden prompt set and regression suite, scoring approach, and timeline.

[05:00] Samira Lopez: to start success criteria, teams often use a weighted rubric. recommended dimensions: factual accuracy / hallucination rate, format adherence (structured output), latency (p95 under target), and human rater score for usefulness. for healthcare we suggest putting higher weight on hallucination/factual accuracy, like 40-50%.
[05:25] Maya Chen: that makes sense, Aaron what is your tolerance?
[05:28] Dr. Aaron Patel: ideally <2% hallucination on clinical facts for the pilot, and formatting errors less than 5% because downstream parsers break. if we hit those numbers we will consider expanding.

[08:10] Evan Martinez: good, we can target that. workload sizing — do you have expected QPS and typical sequence lengths?
[08:18] Luke Howard: peak is roughly 30 qps across the fleet, average prompt length ~250 tokens, but some summaries run to 1k tokens. for the benchmark we can provide mixes: 70% short Q&A (<=300 tokens), 30% long summaries (~800-1000 tokens).
[08:36] Samira Lopez: perfect, for the quality eval we typically run: 1k queries for an initial benchmark across 2-3 model variants, plus a focused 200-sample human-eval set for golden prompt scoring.

[12:00] Dr. Aaron Patel: on golden prompts — we want examples that represent edge cases: atypical phrasing, mixed languages, shorthand notes, and overlapping meds. can you describe how Redwood defines a golden prompt and golden answer?
[12:10] Samira Lopez: yes — golden prompts are representative input examples selected by the customer; golden answers are human-verified outputs we expect the model to produce (format and factual content). Redwood will store the golden set in the eval harness and run automated comparisons: exact match where required, fuzzy match for free-text, and structured field checks for parsed outputs.
[12:35] Maya Chen: what about hallucinations that are subtle, like invented drug interactions? how do you detect those automatically?
[12:42] Samira Lopez: detection is two-tiered: automated heuristics (entity consistency checks, cross-checks vs patient record fields) plus human review on a sampled subset. we also run fact-checking against a curated knowledge base when possible. automated flags mark likely hallucinations for rater review.

[17:00] Evan Martinez: we should clarify scoring approach. proposal: weighted score = 0.5 * factuality_score + 0.2 * format_score + 0.2 * rater_score + 0.1 * latency_score, with pass threshold at 0.8 for pilot. does that align?
[17:18] Dr. Aaron Patel: curious how you compute factuality_score numerically.
[17:22] Samira Lopez: factuality_score is 1 - hallucination_rate for the eval set; hallucination detection uses annotation labels from human raters plus automated flags. for example if 3% hallucinations across the golden set, factuality_score = 0.97. we then normalize to 0-1.
[17:40] Maya Chen: rater_score is subjective; what scale and inter-rater agreement?
[17:45] Samira Lopez: we use a 1-5 Likert where 4+ is acceptable; rater_score will be averaged and normalized to 0-1. we recommend at least 3 raters per item for agreement checks.

[22:00] Luke Howard: on benchmarks — we want both hosted and dedicated runs. can Redwood run the 1k query benchmark on hosted first, then run the same on a dedicated pool with quantized models to compare cost/latency tradeoffs?
[22:20] Evan Martinez: yes, that s standard. we will schedule hosted baseline, then dedicated runs. note that quantized model variants may change hallucination characteristics slightly — we will include those in regression tests.

[26:30] Maya Chen: format checks — important. outputs must follow JSON schema we provide. how do you validate schema compliance and handle partial/invalid outputs?
[26:42] Samira Lopez: we validate with a strict JSON schema parser in the harness. outputs that fail schema are counted as format_errors; we capture partial parseable fields too and score those separately. format_score = 1 - (format_error_rate).

[30:00] Dr. Aaron Patel: timeline? we need pilot decisions by end of Q2.
[30:06] Evan Martinez: proposed timeline: this week exchange prompts/samples, week of 2026-05-11 run 1k benchmark and dedicated runs, week of 2026-05-18 we deliver full eval report + rater results, decision meeting 2026-05-22.
[30:24] Maya Chen: tight but doable.

[34:00] Samira Lopez: regression tests — we recommend building a regression suite of ~200 golden examples that must pass on every model change. tests include: exact matches for structured fields, fuzzy similarity >0.85 for free text (bert-sim or rouge depending), and no hallucinated entities. failing tests should block promotion.
[34:30] Evan Martinez: also we will surface model deltas: token-level differences and example-level diff reports so you can see regressions.

[38:00] Sofia Ramos: security question: for dedicated runs will audit logs include token-level tracing and who accessed what? and KMS integration for keys?
[38:12] Evan Martinez: dedicated includes audit logs with request metadata; for token-level we can show hashed tokens and truncated traces in logs for compliance. KMS/HSM integration is supported and we can add it in the private deployment if needed.

[41:00] Luke Howard: latency targets: we need p95 < 600ms for Q&A and <2s for long summaries. is that realistic with 1k token outputs?
[41:12] Samira Lopez: for 1k token generation p95 under 2s is aggressive but achievable on dedicated GPU pools with proper batching and KV cache warmups; hosted may be higher depending on load. we will include latency SLO checks in the benchmark.

[45:00] Dr. Aaron Patel: how do you handle data residency/PHI in hosted mode?
[45:08] Evan Martinez: hosted API can be configured with data retention off for PII, and we offer Dedicated/Private where data never leaves your VPC. we ll include SOC2 / ISO docs and a redacted security questionnaire in the packet.

[48:00] Maya Chen: scoring thresholds — can we run sensitivity analysis? e.g., show how overall weighted score moves if hallucination rate moves from 2% to 5%?
[48:12] Samira Lopez: yes we ll include a sensitivity table in the report and show breakpoints where pass/fail flips. we also produce per-scenario scoring to show which prompt categories are weak.

[52:00] Evan Martinez: technical note on hallucination detection: sometimes hallucinations are plausible-sounding but incorrect — automated checks flag entities that are inconsistent with patient record (e.g., drug A listed but not in prior med list). those flags are then human-reviewed. we try to minimize false positives by tuning heuristics per dataset.

[55:00] Maya Chen: ok recap please and next steps.
[55:10] Evan Martinez: recap: next steps — Novamed to provide 200 representative prompts + 50 golden answers by 2026-05-07; Redwood to send initial golden prompt template and full scoring rubric by 2026-05-05; Redwood to run hosted baseline and dedicated quantized runs week of 2026-05-11 (1k queries + 200 human-eval), deliver report week of 2026-05-18; security docs and questionnaire to be shared by Redwood in two business days.
[55:45] Dr. Aaron Patel: thanks, please include explicit examples of hallucinations you ll look for and how they re labeled.
[55:52] Samira Lopez: will do, we ll include example labels (hallucinated_entity, incorrect_date, wrong_med_dosage, format_failure) in the rubric.
[56:04] Sofia Ramos: and please cc compliance on the security packet.
[56:08] Evan Martinez: noted, will cc.
[56:15] Maya Chen: great thanks everyone.
[56:18] Evan Martinez: thanks all, end call.
